# Parser code-review skill

Guidance for reviewing simulation-parser pull requests in this repository. Apply
it when a PR adds or reworks a parser under `src/nomad_simulation_parsers/parsers/`
or its tests under `tests/parsers/`. The authoritative source is
`docs/how_to/test_parsers.md`; this is the review-oriented distillation.

## Architecture

A parser is tested as a pipeline:
`files -> recognition -> source reader -> parsed source data -> mapper -> archive`,
with `normalizer` branching off the archive. Extraction and mapping must be
**independently callable**: the reader turns a source fragment into parsed data;
the `ArchiveWriter`/transformers turn parsed data into an archive fragment, with
**no file access or `self.data` reach-in inside the transformers**. Flag any
transformer that re-reads files or re-walks fixed paths internally instead of
receiving its inputs as arguments.

## Required test files

Under `tests/parsers/<code>/` — call out any missing when a parser is added or
reworked:

- `test_recognition.py` (`@pytest.mark.unit`) — mainfile/auxiliary matching and
  rejection via `is_mainfile`, using a temp dir. **Must not create an
  `EntryArchive`.**
- `test_reader.py` (`@pytest.mark.unit`) — call the lowest-level reader on a
  **minimal inline fragment** and assert parsed **semantic values with units**
  (not just presence/counts). One fixture per syntax feature; include truncated,
  malformed-numeric, repeated-section, optional-field, and line-ending cases.
- `test_mapping.py` (`@pytest.mark.unit`) — feed **hand-built parsed data**
  directly to the mapping transformers / `ArchiveWriter`. No reader, no
  normalizer.
- `test_integration.py` (`@pytest.mark.integration`) — compose the shared suites
  `SimulationParserTestSuite` + `WorkflowTestSuite` from `tests.parsers.common`;
  one subclass per calculation mode; add only a short list of identifying values.
- `test_pipeline.py` (`@pytest.mark.pipeline`) — subclass
  `SimulationParserPipelineTestSuite` with the same fixture and program name.

## Mapping-contract checks (Layer 3)

Every supported archive concept needs a test covering: (a) target section type
and path; (b) value and explicit unit conversion; (c) array shape and index/spin
ordering; (d) references between systems, methods, outputs, and workflow tasks;
(e) the **absent vs empty vs 0 vs False** distinction; (f) merge or precedence
rules when multiple files supply the same concept.

## Markers and fixtures

- Markers: `unit` (recognition/reader/mapping/utility), `integration` (public
  entry point), `pipeline` (parser + normalizers), `large_fixture` (fixtures too
  big for the default checkout).
- Reader/mapping fragments inline or < 10 KiB; integration fixtures small and
  representative. **Large fixtures must carry `@pytest.mark.large_fixture`** and
  never be silently skipped. Prefer the smallest source the real reader accepts;
  redact machine/user paths.

## Negative and metamorphic tests (required)

Each parser needs negative tests for a truncated mainfile, a missing required
side file, and invalid content, each with an explicit expected behavior
(exception, warning with partial archive, or ignored optional file). Add
metamorphic tests where applicable: line-ending invariance, unit rescaling,
atom translation preserving energies.

## Red flags

- A single whole-parser test over a large fixture used as the *primary* test —
  too broad to locate failures; the boundary (reader/mapping) tests are missing.
- No `unit`-layer tests (recognition/reader/mapping): the PR fast gate then
  exercises nothing for the parser.
- Conditional assertions such as `if output.electronic_dos:` — if a fixture
  promises a section, its absence must fail the test.
- Serialized archives or snapshot objects used as oracles; expected data
  generated by running the parser under test in CI.
- Normalization behavior asserted inside parser tests (keep it in the pipeline
  layer).
- Copying the parser-independent parts of the shared suites into a parser
  instead of subclassing `tests.parsers.common`.
